totiens: totiēns (adv.) — so often, so many times
transverberat: trānsverberō, -āre — to pierce through, transfix (3rd sg. pres.)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumuli: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, burial mound, tomb (gen. sg.)
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
tyranni: tyrannus, -ī (m.) — ruler, despot, tyrant (gen. sg.) · also m. nom. pl. (tyrannī, the rulers)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent)
utque: ut (conj.) — that, so that, as, when (+ -que 'and')
venientis: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (pres. part., f. gen. sg., with fāmae) · also m. acc. pl. in -is = -ēs (venientis pellere, those coming)
vibranti: vibrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to brandish, make flash, quiver (pres. part., m./n. abl. sg., with gladiō)
vidit: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. perf.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
vocant: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd pl. pres.)
volans: volō, -āre — to fly (pres. part., m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (columba volāns)
volnus: vulnus (volnus), vulneris (n.) — wound (acc./nom. sg.; older spelling)
volucri: volucris, -is — winged, swift; (f.) bird (adj./noun, m./f./n. abl. sg.; dat. sg.)
volvit: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, roll along (3rd sg. pres.)
